key_insight: PISA is a preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM optimizer for deep models that provably converges under minimal assumptions while flexibly supporting heterogeneous data and a wide range of preconditioners, yielding practical speed and stability gains.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between theory and practice for training deep networks on heterogeneous or ill-conditioned data by providing an ADMM-based optimizer that allows inexact updates and arbitrary preconditioners without sacrificing convergence guarantees.
method: Formulate deep-model training within a preconditioned, inexact stochastic ADMM framework that alternates updates while permitting controlled inexactness.
Introduce flexible preconditioners (task- or layer-specific) into ADMM updates to improve conditioning and per-iteration progress.
Prove convergence under minimal assumptions and validate empirically across diverse tasks, showing faster/stabler training versus standard optimizers.
impact: Allows ML practitioners to plug in problem-specific preconditioners and use ADMM-style updates with theoretical assurances, improving training speed and robustness for federated, multimodal, and ill-conditioned scenarios.
visual_elements: Algorithm flow diagram: alternating ADMM updates with a highlighted preconditioner block and inexact update arrow
Performance chart: convergence curves comparing PISA vs Adam/SGD across multiple tasks (faster loss decrease, fewer epochs)
Schematic of heterogeneous setup: multiple data sources or federated nodes feeding into a single model with different preconditioners
Benefit icons strip: theoretical guarantees, flexible preconditioning, empirical speedup, robustness
paper_title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
paper_authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
